subject: project:gdl
value: gdlmem stale's `reopen_candidates` list was NOT a queue of under-documented conversion caps: on 2026-09-01 all 43 entries were false positives, and the list was measuring how thoroughly a park had been VERIFIED and LAW-SCREENED rather than what it was about. Root cause, read directly from memory_graph/core.py attempt_staleness(): the heuristic matched `conversion_terms` against `attempted_axis + raw_json`, i.e. the WHOLE record JSON. Three independent leaks, each counted by hand against the 43: (1) 31/43 matched the substring 'defake' supplied by the MANDATORY gate command quoted in `attributes.verification` ('defake_gate.py check', 'defake_gate baseline') - so following AGENTS.md's required gate discipline is what flagged the park; (2) 13/43 matched the bare substring 'cast' occurring inside CITED LAW IDs in `attributes.law_screen` (cast-transit, cast-view-macro, typed-global-member-vs-view-cast-diverges, noop-cast-on-array-decay) or in axis prose such as 'volatile cast' - screening the law corpus is what flagged the park; (3) 3/43 matched 'raw-offset' inside explicitly NEGATED prose ('none applicable: no raw-offset conversion at this site'), i.e. the park was flagged for the exact class it had ruled out. The implementation contradicted its own inline comment ('form-undocumented only applies to parks about FIELD-CONVERSION work - scheduler/regalloc parks document different axes'): by residual_class the 43 were 17 STRUCTURAL, 11 REGISTER_ONLY, 5 SCHEDULE, 2 STACK_LAYOUT, 1 MIXED and zero conversion caps. A second, independent defect in the same test: `form_terms` is a five-word whitelist (offsetof / typed alias / repeated cast / inline cast / declared alias), so a park that documents its failing form as 'the arm-swapped ternary', 'block-scope cursor' or 'staging local' scores as form-UNDOCUMENTED. CORRECTED QUEUE, derived independently by age-screening the same 43 against the law wave: 37/43 records already carry an explicit `attributes.law_screen` naming 2-11 wave laws, several exhaustively (WPitchMat3 v5 screened all six brief-named laws with per-law measured refutations). Only 6 records predate 2026-08-31 and could not have screened the wave - camera_mode_level, StartThrowMagicFX, PlayerProcessPowerups (all 2026-08-29), CaptionTextSub, do_shop, do_shopping_8009AA48 (all 2026-08-30) - and the last two are shop.c, owned by another lane this run. The genuine reopen queue was therefore FOUR functions, not 42, and driving it produced one real improvement (PlayerProcessPowerups 98.60 -> 99.10 fuzzy) and one byte-identical de-fakematch (CaptionTextSub). FIX LANDED (commit 317fb36c0): the conversion test now reads a substance-only projection of the record (`_park_substance_text`, excluding verification/law_screen/laws_applied/anchors/scope/history_screen/measurement_resolution/provenance), bare 'cast' is removed from conversion_terms, and `_mentions_unnegated` suppresses negated mentions; the FORM test deliberately still reads the whole record, because law_screen legitimately documents forms tried. Measured effect on the live corpus: reopen_candidates 43 -> 4, with memory_graph/test_graph.py's two pinned behaviours (attempt.formless.v1 flagged, attempt.schedpark.v1 not flagged) still green. GENERAL LESSON for any future record-mining heuristic: never match tool names or cited record ids as evidence about a record's subject - a project whose discipline requires quoting its gate commands and citing its law corpus will make every well-run session look like the thing being searched for, and the resulting queue is anti-correlated with the work it claims to rank.
